findings.title: Kinship can train care but cannot answer in another person’s place
findings.claim: The parent-child bond named in the warning is the strongest imaginable human proxy, while the earlier family sequence makes care and gratitude concrete; the focus therefore turns protective responsibility back to each person without making kinship worthless.
findings.mechanism: The focus joins self-protection and a paired denial of substitution. The wider family sequence supplies pregnancy, repeated weakness, gratitude, bounded obedience, and continued companionship; these contacts make the protective imperative a personal answer formed within relationships rather than inherited shelter.
findings.reader_payoff: The family warning limits proxy rather than canceling care: closeness may nurture a person, but cannot perform that person’s response.
findings.containment: The causal step from nurture to mature self-guarding is an inference, not a claim that parenting guarantees it. The live alternative is that 31:33 addresses final substitution only; the contextual reading leaves that primary warning intact.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch meanings are supplied by trusted evidence; the wider family sequence is an exact but legacy-attributed HFT trace, so the developmental link remains qualified.

findings.title: The promised day gives present protection a fixed horizon
findings.claim: The focus presents the promise as true and time-bound, and the wider promise-and-truth recurrence places it beside enduring reward and an appointed Day of Decision; future certainty is therefore a present claim on conduct.
findings.mechanism: The focus promise and truth words meet the commands to protect oneself and fear the day. Their recurrence in 31:9 beside abiding gardens and in 35:5 with the same warning, together with 44:40’s appointed Day of Decision, links assurance, timing, and current action.
findings.reader_payoff: The promise is not only news about later events: its reliability gives present protective choices a horizon while holding warning and hope together.
findings.containment: The repeated formula may independently certify local propositions rather than deliberately echo. The well-constructed-statement branch is not retained because its specialist facet would require its unsupported textile core; truth and appointed-time readings remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The focus truth and promise are trusted; wider exact-surface echoes and contextual timing include legacy-attributed evidence, so intentional recall is not asserted.

findings.title: Near life offers real goods without securing the whole horizon
findings.claim: The worldly life in the focus remains real and beneficial, yet its nearness, first appearance, and uncertain completion can be mistaken for a guarantee of the whole outcome.
findings.mechanism: The focus pairs nearer life with the repeated deception warning. The wider contrast of 87:16–17 favors the Hereafter as more enduring, 57:20 depicts worldly growth fading, and 31:20 pairs outward and inward blessings; these triggers make proximity and visibility evidence of a real but partial good rather than final security.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning need not call worldly goods false: the danger is treating what is near, first, and visible as the complete future.
findings.containment: The hereafter contrast does not make ordinary benefit unreal. The exact deception mechanism remains open: the warning may target temporal overvaluation, unsupported argument, or both.

epistemic.reason: Trusted cross-run evidence is independently reinforced by exact supplied Arabic in wider ayat; some surface-bias detail is legacy-attributed and bounded.

findings.title: Two warnings expose practical and religious confidence
findings.claim: The focus distinguishes confidence drawn from worldly appearance from confidence produced by a deceiver speaking about God; wider examples show that each can hide a different uncertainty.
findings.mechanism: The first focus clause makes worldly life the deceiving agent; the second names a deceiver in relation to God. False assurance about punishment in 3:24 and false hopes in 57:14 return to these clauses, allowing practical attraction and religious misassurance to be seen as related but distinct routes.
findings.reader_payoff: A reader can notice both what looks safe in ordinary life and what claims spiritual safety without warrant.
findings.containment: Receiver-side simplicity is a contextual account of vulnerability, not a label for every addressee. The passages illustrate false assurance without claiming all religious trust is deception.

epistemic.reason: The focus claim is trusted; receiver vulnerability is legacy-attributed and wider connections supply no target morphology.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Yaşam işlerinde denenmemiş, az deneyimli ve kötülüğü sezmekte yetersiz olma durumudur.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: 3:24 and 57:14 show hearers relying on false assurance and hope
branch_activations.activation: The receiver relation makes inexperience or weak detection available as a vulnerability; the wider examples supply cases without making it the lexical meaning of the deceiver.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The two routes can exploit an unguarded receiver-state.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not call every addressee naive or gullible.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişiyi yalan haber veya gerçeğe uymayan görünüşle bilerek yanıltma eylemidir.

branch_activations.activation: The outside assurances return through the focus root’s two clauses, distinguishing worldly confidence from confidence about God.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Practical attraction and religious misassurance are related without becoming one generic warning.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus critiques deception, not all worldly goods or religious claims.

findings.title: Even what comes through lineage remains within account
findings.claim: The focus denies substitution in both directions, and its indefinite thing can include a knowable item while the parent-child relation names what is generated through lineage; 31:16 extends this to hidden and minute matters.
findings.mechanism: The focus thing and parent-child terms meet 31:16’s weighed mustard seed, hidden location, and retrieval. Lineage is a generated relation, but neither it nor the smallest knowable matter escapes the focus’s no-substitution scope.
findings.reader_payoff: The no-proxy warning reaches both relationships and the smallest reportable matter without turning family relation into a payment mechanism.
findings.containment: The knowable-thing source image is an attributed candidate variant, not a verified lexicon facet. 31:16 may demonstrate power and knowledge without specifying final accounting; that alternative remains live.

epistemic.reason: The knowable and generated readings come from legacy candidate evidence; 31:16 supplies exact HFT anchor text but its mapped branches remain attributed.

findings.title: Real benefit and reliable promise remain in the same warning

findings.mechanism: The life-as-benefit carrier meets 31:20’s outward and inward blessings; the truth predicate and promise meet 31:9’s gardens and repeated formula. Their contact makes the promise a stable counter-horizon to real but limited benefit.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader need not choose between appreciating worldly good and hearing the warning; the contrast concerns what can secure the final horizon.
findings.containment: The countermeasure is an interpretive relation, not detailed chronology. The 31:9 recurrence may certify its local proposition independently.

epistemic.reason: This legacy-attributed candidate is grounded by exact 31:9 and 31:20 surfaces, but the synthesis remains inferential.

findings.title: Distraction can precede the focus warning about deception
findings.claim: The focus’s repeated deception warning can be read beside an earlier sequence in which renewed diversion occupies attention, failed uptake follows, and hearing is pictured as blocked.
findings.mechanism: The focus lure is the return point. In 31:6 occupation by amusement and renewed speech appear together; in 31:7 refusal to heed is followed by weight in the ear. The sequence supplies an attentional path that may make deception easier to sustain.
findings.reader_payoff: The warning may concern conditions that keep a misleading surface from being tested, not only assent to a false proposition.
findings.containment: The HFT marks the arrow from attention capture to susceptibility as inference. The sequence may instead diagnose obstinate refusal without explaining deception’s mechanics; context-root readings remain attributed.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace names exact anchors, indices, roots, and roles, but target morphology is absent and the causal arrow is explicitly inferential.
